Approach: the J2 engine (14 modules, 16.4k lines, baseline J2 ce2631f) is copied in place into sutra_app/engine/ with package-relative imports and eleven numbered patches (P1-P11); llm.py becomes a shim over one ModelPort.complete(CompletionRequest) seam whose call syntax is unchanged (ask(system, user, mock, max_tokens, effort, on_progress, json_mode, images, schema) plus a CallTag with run, department, function, stage, step, atom, purpose); J2's mock mode is the stub-connector path through the 'scripted' callable, with a built-in ScriptedPort so the engine can be built before the connectors. D9 is confirmed with evidence (module state measured: a second run in one process flipped item_kind from form to doc_section; NAMES, ROUTES, RATES, OUTPUT, llm.LAST_META are process globals). The process contract is the orchestrator's: python -m sutra_app.engine --run-dir, task.json and inbox.jsonl in, events.jsonl out with exactly the event types and fields of ORCH 5.6, a 5 s heartbeat, SQLite never touched. Because the process cannot be asked questions, it also publishes snapshot.json and live.json so the 25 GET and 5 POST J2 endpoints (one views.py, a FastAPI adapter and a stdlib adapter) read files; routes are mounted both under /d/{dept}/ and at the root with ?dept= because the orchestrator and UI sections disagree. Function nodes plug in through EngineHooks (observe-only; system_addendum is the only prompt-changing hook, empty by default). Tests: three legacy J2 scripts run as subprocess suites with guards (measured here on Python 3.11: change_test 192 checks, realization_test 97; the flow script cannot pass on the J2 checkout itself without its saved runs), plus recorded goldens for prompts and API shapes. Six work packages E0-E5; j2.py is owned by E1 alone. Key trade-offs: files instead of pipes (survives a server restart, matches ORCH, costs a 250 ms publish lag); finished-run follow-ups use rehydrate, proven only for the classic path in mock mode (realization-on, J2's default, paused in two attempts; cause not found), otherwise they start fresh with the old files as context; engine keeps its own vendored artifact models and rules next to the library's port, with a drift test. No question blocks development; the consolidator must settle: (1) /d/{dept} prefix vs ?dept= (both mounted), (2) one copy of artifact models/rules/template bases (engine vs library DL9), (3) make_port(PortSpec) wording in connectors.md (spec.mock instead of spec.model.mode), (4) the orchestrator's stop_live call and its seven-key RunSpec.settings allowlist.

summary:
Wrote the connectors section (511 lines) at ~/Desktop/development/sutra-pro/docs/design/connectors.md and 46 scrubbed fixtures under ~/Desktop/development/sutra-pro/tests/fixtures/connectors/ (21 captured from real claude 2.1.308 and codex-cli 0.146.0, 25 derived and labelled in MANIFEST.json; I spent two real calls per CLI, the rest needed no model). Nothing else in the repo was edited.

Approach: one Router picks a provider per call from a versioned data policy (default = J2 behaviour: Claude first, Codex only as fallback), checks installed, signed-in and quota state without a model call, enforces a per-request Allowance computed by the caller, and runs a ModelConnector child (Claude: claude -p stream-json, Codex: codex exec --json, one process per call or turn, environment allowlist, prompt on stdin). Structured JSON goes native first (--json-schema, --output-schema through a strict-schema adapter), then prompted with a pydantic repair loop. The router emits one UsageIn per step into the orchestrator's UsageSink; tokens are the comparable unit, usd is Claude's list-price estimate (Codex only with owner-supplied rates). Tool connectors: one stdlib MCP server with read-only Sutra tools plus gh-backed GitHub read tools, usable by both CLIs; Claude-held Gmail, Drive and Slack are shown only (ADR-035). A StubConnector (honours J2's mock callable) and fake claude/codex/gh executables replay the fixtures. D7 is confirmed: the Anthropic-API and Gemini providers are not carried over (CD1).

Findings that shaped the design (all probed): (1) usage counters are CUMULATIVE on resumed sessions in both CLIs (Claude total_cost_usd and modelUsage, Codex turn.completed.usage) while Claude result.usage is per turn, so the ledger must store deltas; (2) a signed-out Codex call retries 401 for about 18 s before failing, so sign-in is checked first and two 401 events abort early; (3) Claude marks failures with is_error true but subtype success, and classifies them in assistant.error; (4) --safe-mode drops --mcp-config servers while --restricted keeps them; (5) a bad --effort is only a warning; (6) codex exec resume takes no -s or -C; (7) this shell leaks about 30 CLAUDE_CODE_* variables and GITHUB_TOKEN, so an allowlist, not J2's denylist, is required.

Contracts aligned with the sibling sections as they stood: engine ModelPort/CallTag/ModelError and make_port, orchestrator ConnectorPort (including records_usage and set_provider with model) and UsageSink, library transport schemas, UI provider chip and 503 text. Proposed agreements A1-A4 are listed in section 9.

Questions for the owner or consolidator: (a) approve changing the diagram text "ChatGPT login or API key in the keychain" to "ChatGPT login (API-key login refused unless allowed)" (CD13) and "installed and signed in through Sutra" to "installed on this Mac, signed in through Sutra" (CD17); (b) A1/A2: who writes the usage row for engine runs (the engine's usage event versus the router's sink; both are idempotent through call_ref) and the nullable detail_json column; (c) final D-numbers for CD1-CD18. UNVERIFIED and left to live tests: Codex strict schema against the real API, Codex image input, real model tool calls over MCP on either CLI, --max-budget-usd behaviour, claude mcp list output (not run: it mutates Claude state). Probe leftovers outside the repo (two small sessions) are listed with their removal commands in section 1.2.

summary: Wrote docs/design/library.md (about 625 lines, 18 sections). Approach: every structure is a closed pydantic v2 class in three tiers (Value, Record with kind + schema_version, registered Payload), strict and frozen, with evolve() as the only update. One registry keyed by (family, version) with kind as discriminator exports JSON Schemas to docs/schemas/ and diffs them in tests. One write gate (Gate.check -> Checked: strict validation, cross rules, canonical JSON, sha256, round trip) is the only way stores accept data, enforced by an AST test. Model output is parsed tolerantly (J2 extract_json, enum case, unknown keys dropped and recorded) and then validated strictly; transport schemas are generated from the same class with J2's const-dropping bug fixed (const becomes enum) and unions rewritten as anyOf. The org chart is one tree document; a single ChartChange (kind reuse/add/rearrange derived from ops and checked) uses $ref placeholders, code-assigned ids, ids kept on rearrange (merged ids become aliases), a department always carrying its five function node ids, and carry_links so no chat session is dropped. The Atom is the plugin's atom (goal, constraints, context, work, verify) plus J2's expected_output and checks, with states open, closed, refused, abandoned (verify_failed is an outcome, derived in the atom/1 view), a ledger row and cards; Node is an abstract base with StructuralNode and FunctionNode and five function children, with function specifics entering as data (FunctionSpecs) because spec-function-nodes.json did not exist (checked three times). Workflow/Step are two-level bases (TaskWorkflow of AssignmentSteps; DeptWorkflow of AIStep/CodeStep atoms); J2 artifact models and rules are ported strict+frozen and registered as 22 payloads; every J2 run file maps to a family through gate_record (log mode first, strict after a golden-run test). Core mechanics were prototyped on pydantic 2.14.2 and every rejection in the test table was observed. Key trade-offs: strictness against real model output (mitigated by the tolerant parser), stored refused atoms (extra to the plugin), one change class instead of three. Decisions needed before development: (1) spec-function-nodes.json still missing, FunctionSpec names are a proposal; (2) orchestrator.md plans its own Closed/OrgChart/ChartChange/gate() in the same paths (library/base.py, org_chart.py) with parent_id/archive/version and node ids f:<dept>:<fn>, edge kinds has_function/reads/rework, AtomOut.state verify_failed: the consolidator must pick one owner (recommended: the library's models, with section 18 listing every difference); (3) confirm the owner wants refused atoms stored and ledgered; (4) raise the pydantic pin to >=2.11 in pyproject; (5) a live test must confirm the Claude CLI accepts const-as-enum and anyOf of objects.

summary: Wrote docs/design/orchestrator.md (540 lines; module paths below are relative to ~/Desktop/development/sutra-pro). Approach: one org-chat session (cs_org) talks to the chat agent, which handles each owner request in at most three structured stages (decide, then the library's chart-change class, then assignments). Every reply is a flat class with its own transport schema, checked with ReplyParser, GATE and the library's apply_change dry run (all violations), plus our guards (reuse-first, retired id, busy). It retries up to 3 times per stage, then falls back to a keyword planner. ChartStore.apply is the single chart writer: it appends org_charts, projects org_nodes and org_edges, builds graph nodes and chat sessions together, and logs every decision (even a reuse) as a chart_changes row with a sha chain. The graph never stores the tree: contains, has_function and has_step are derived on read. Departments are fixed once created (library DL5); divisions move, merge and split, and merge and split ask the owner first. A department's chat is Identity only; its questions appear as needs_you cards in the org chat but are answered in the department session; function and step chats are read-only. Runs follow the protocol the engine section has adopted: task.json and inbox.jsonl in, events.jsonl out, one process per run, SQLite written by the server only. A RunWatcher projects events in one transaction with events_offset. The 14-table DDL, the reply classes and the SSE route were executed and verified (SQLite 3.51, pydantic 2.14, FastAPI 0.162). Key trade-offs: up to six model calls for a new team (one for a reuse); merge and split ask first (veto-able); statuses are J2 map words with a separate outcome column because the library's Node.state has only five words; one live task per department. No question blocks development; the open items for the consolidator are L-1, L-2, E-1, U-1 and U-2 (see open_risks), and the function-node spec file never landed (checked five times).

decision_proposals.decision: Two kinds of chat, one voice each: the org chat (cs_org, the Root node's session) talks to the chat agent 'Sutra'; a department's chat is Identity only (the owner's lines and Identity's to_user lines, as J2's Simple view); team questions show as needs_you cards in the org chat but are answered in the department session, never by the chat agent; a division chat is a filtered view of its tasks' lines; function and step chats are read-only (403).

decision_proposals.rejected: The chat agent relaying or rewriting Identity's words; one merged chat for everything; routing owner text into function agents (breaks the single voice).

summary: Design section for the UI, 558 lines, written after reading J2 (page, server, harnesses, schemas), the plugin atom, draw.io page 3, gen.py and the orchestrator, library and engine sections. Approach: two pages in one look. A new Home page at `/` (J2's Simple skeleton) holds the org chat (session `cs_org`) on the left and the Workflow graph, Org chart and Settings on the right, with the rail listing the teams. The J2 page is copied once and served per department at `/d/{dept id}/` with 12 small, scripted, tested edits. J2's routes keep their root paths and a `fetch` wrapper adds `?dept=`, matching the orchestrator and engine sections. The graph and org chart are drawn by pure layout and SVG functions that reuse J2's edge CSS, tokens and look, with live updates from SSE events that trigger a refetch, and a polling fallback. One drawer, `#nodepanel`, built on J2's Agent-drawer pattern, holds the per-node chat and the function-node details (goal, task, context, work atoms with state and verify, who it hands to). Home's hand-over is the `task` card that links to the department's Simple view. Checked here: all 12 edits apply with the stated match counts; the ported page printed byte-identical output to J2's own two node harnesses (612,427 and 152,504 bytes); in headless Chrome 156 under `/d/org_…/` there were zero CSP messages and zero failed loads, the Map drew, and every J2 call carried `dept=`. Chrome drives over CDP with `websockets` (already installed), and `node --test` needs a file list or a quoted glob (a directory argument fails). Main trade-offs: the department is in the page path (J2 rewrites `location.search`), J2's runtime edge router is not reused (it needs `getBBox` and is absent on Home), and fonts are not vendored. Needs a decision or reconciliation: who serves the J2 page (engine row 1 vs this UI), the `sutra_app.web` vs `sutra_app.ui` name, the write token as header or cookie, three small additions to the orchestrator payloads, and the still-missing function-node spec.

open_risks: Cross-section reconciliation needed: the engine section serves the J2 page at GET / with a sutra_dept cookie, while here GET / is Home and the J2 page is /d/{dept id}/ (GET /?dept= redirects there); the engine's pages.py should be dropped or call render_page, and paths.ui_dir() should return sutra_app.ui.PAGES_DIR.

The web package name (orchestrator imports sutra_app.web, the UI is sutra_app.ui; UI-1 ships a one-line alias), the boot injector name (inject_boot vs render_page), and the services attributes mount() reads (settings.token, version, a department lookup) are assumed and unconfirmed.

Write token: the orchestrator injects X-Sutra-Token into the page, the engine expects a cookie accepted by write_guard; the UI sends the header on every non-GET and the browser sends any cookie by itself, so the server must accept either.

Three small requests to the orchestrator (each with a UI fallback): ChartChangeOut gets task_title and the node-id lists added, moved, archived, reused; GraphView.nodes comes parents first with siblings in position order; a function node's meta carries goal, task, context, wait_on, last_seen and hands_to.

The function-node spec file (spec-function-nodes.json) was still absent at the last check; Goal, Task and Context rest on the library's FunctionNode fields and the open atom behind one adapter, FnodeView.normalize.

The copied J2 page will keep changing upstream (latest J2 commit 2026-11-03); the port script's per-edit match counts and --check detect drift, and the byte-parity test needs goldens captured once with J2 present from a small state fixture (a finished run's state is 856 KB).

J2's own stdlib server compares POST paths exactly, so a POST with ?dept= got 404 in my probe against J2's server; the engine's FastAPI routes accept the query, so this only matters when the page is served against J2's server.
Fonts are not vendored, so offline typography falls back to Arial and Menlo; the CSP needs 'unsafe-inline' for scripts and styles because the J2 page script is one 3,000-line inline script.

Browser tooling: Chrome 156 over CDP is the only browser tried; websockets 17 warns unless connect() is used as a context manager; the Playwright cached headless shell and safaridriver are untried; browser tests skip when Chrome is absent. node --test needs a file list or a quoted glob on Node 25 (a directory argument fails).

Two sources of one conversation (J2's run folder and the department session): if they differ in length the J2 pane and the node panel may differ; a graph above 500 nodes falls back to the List view without virtualisation; the department page keeps J2's 700 ms poll of a large state.
pyproject.toml has no package-data for sutra_app/ui/pages and ui/static, so a built wheel would miss the HTML, JS and CSS (editable installs work; file owned elsewhere).
Not designed: ?embed=1 (the Simple view inside Home), font vendoring, drag-to-pin in the new graph, and any chart editing from the page.
